body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}=\widehat Q^I_{0t,\ell}-\sum_{j=1}^J\widehat w_{\ell j}\widehat Q_{jt,\ell}\), with \(Q^N_{0t,\ell}=\sum_{j=1}^Jw_{\ell j}Q_{jt,\ell}\), exact finite-array loss \(m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}+n_\ell^{-1}A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}\) plus the three displayed \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) terms, and conditional squared-radius calibration \(a_\ell c^*(\eta,\alpha)\)

sampling_model.design: Fixed \(J\), \(T_0\), and \(T_1\) repeated-cross-section distributional synthetic-control panel in which one simplex weight \(w_\ell\) spans the treated no-intervention quantile law in every pre-treatment and post-treatment panel period.
sampling_model.units: The treated and donor cell laws are fixed primitives; each pre cell contributes \(n_\ell\) independent draws and each post cell contributes \(m_\ell\) independent draws.
sampling_model.treatment: Only unit \(j=0\) is intervened upon after period \(T_0\); donor post laws and \(F^I_{0t,\ell}\) are observed, while \(F^N_{0t,\ell}\) is the post-treatment no-intervention counterfactual identified by the same \(w_\ell\) learned from pre-treatment periods.
sampling_model.overlap: No atom-mass lower bound, post-knot separation, interior-weight restriction, or restriction on \(n_\ell/m_\ell\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pre quantiles, the simplex weight, the finite-array Gram \(H_\ell\), score covariance, post multinomial masses, support clusters, and within-cell offset differences are estimated with simultaneous confidence regions; within-cell differences become exactly observed coordinates in the local experiment, while cross-cell translations and face offsets remain in a certified nuisance region with a rate-preserving fallback. The matrix \(H\) appears only after local-subsequence extraction as a limit of \(H_\ell\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section~5.3.2 and Proposition~5 provide a published discrete distributional-synthetic-control goodness-of-fit limit; its version-of-record formula was not accessible for a finer claim.

The version-of-record Summary states that counterfactuals are identified by matching treated pre-intervention quantile residuals to a convex combination of control residuals orthogonal to observable common factors.
Section~6.2, Assumptions~4--6, and Corollary~3 give DSC inference for smooth continuous empirical quantiles with a donor-dilution condition.
Theorem~2 gives a convergence rate for DSC weights under interior-weight and quantile-draw conditions.
Theorem~2 transforms simultaneous distribution-function bands into valid bands for discrete quantile functions.
The main theorem gives an asymptotically uniformly valid confidence set for a simplex-valued optimizer weight.
Theorem~1 gives uniformly asymptotically valid conditional critical values with a functional nuisance parameter.
Theorem~1 gives finite-sample validity and size exactness for active-rank Gaussian moment-inequality testing.

body.tldr: Exact discrete distributional synthetic control identifies the treated unit's no-intervention quantile law in every pre-treatment and post-treatment panel period with one stable simplex weight. Its QTE estimator has two first-order error sources on different scales: an exact finite-array signed endpoint energy from empirical post-period atoms and a cone-projected quadratic from simplex weight estimation. The exact squared-error decomposition also retains the pre-weight--post-quantile cross term and three donor-quantile remainder terms. Finite-support pulse geometry makes the cross term \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2})\): it has the joint limit \(-2V_h^\top B_t(d,Z)\) at its own \(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}\) scale but vanishes in the normalized loss and all three \(n_\ell/\sqrt{m_\ell}\) phase laws. Uniform identification is imposed on the finite-array Grams \(H_\ell\), while \(H\) appears only as their local-subsequence limit. The project also proves rate-optimal uniformly honest simultaneous \(L^2\) QTE balls and defines the least common deterministic conditional cutoff in a fully specified finite Gaussian experiment. A legal \(J=2\), \(S=2\), \(D=2\) face-plus-collision calculation reduces in its post-dominated restriction to the one-donor Bernoulli 95 percent honesty bracket \((1.913,1.914]\), versus the collision-oracle value \(1.38590382435\); all weight and cross terms vanish in that restriction. The open theorem is a measurable support-cluster and nuisance-region procedure that attains this cutoff while remaining uniformly honest through changing supports, covariance ranks, and simplex faces, with oracle calibration only on separated regular strata.

project_justification.gap: Chen's published DSC identifies counterfactuals by pre-intervention quantile-residual matching, Gunsilius supplies the quantile-span model and discrete goodness-of-fit asymptotics, and Alvarez--Orestes gives direct DSC inference under smooth continuous-cell and donor-dilution conditions. None supplies inference for a post-treatment no-intervention quantile law identified by an exact period-stable span together with the exact atomic-endpoint and local simplex-face experiment, the pulse-sharp generated-weight cross-vector calculation, its three two-sample phases, or a uniformly honest certified common cutoff; no formula-level claim about Gunsilius Proposition~5 is used because its version-of-record equation was inaccessible.
project_justification.niche: Fixed donors, independent pre and post cell samples, one exact span weight across all pre-treatment and post-treatment no-intervention laws, and exact finite-support post laws generate a two-scale experiment. The squared error contains endpoint and face-leading terms plus a pre-weight--post-quantile cross term that is nonzero at its own finer scale but vanishes under every headline normalization. Within-cell mass offsets are asymptotically observed exactly, whereas cross-cell knot translations and local face offsets remain nuisance parameters. Uniform identification is a finite-array condition on \(H_\ell\), while finite diagonal extraction compactifies all scaled gaps and defines \(H\) only as a local-subsequence limit without imposing a new local-array assumption.
project_justification.fill: The theorem program combines the exact six-term finite-array squared-error decomposition, a sharp pulse-geometry bound and joint limit for the pre-weight--post-quantile cross vector, finite-array Gram curvature, the normalized compound loss and three phase laws, exact known-weight and point-mass reductions, the Bernoulli honesty penalty, deterministic conditional-cutoff experiment, legal \(J=2\), \(S=2\), \(D=2\) certificate, and DKW fallback around one falsifiable open target: feasible cutoff attainment with exclusion-budgeted conditional regions and a rate-preserving fallback.

body.related_work: Chen's Journal of Applied Econometrics article is a direct DSC comparator: its version-of-record Summary on p.~505 identifies counterfactuals by matching a vector of treated pre-intervention quantile residuals to a convex combination of control residuals, with residuals orthogonal to observable common factors for poor matching. That residual-factor construction does not state the exact common-weight equality for the treated no-intervention quantile law in every pre-treatment and post-treatment panel period, and it does not supply an atomic-endpoint/simplex-face local experiment or the generated-weight cross-vector limit. Gunsilius establishes the Wasserstein-quantile DSC model for arbitrary one-dimensional outcome laws and gives a discrete goodness-of-fit result in Proposition~5 and Appendix~A.6. The version-of-record full equation was inaccessible in this source check, so the proposal treats Gunsilius as the model and discrete-asymptotic anchor without asserting that its published formula pools knot noise or omits a particular cross term. Alvarez and Orestes are the other direct DSC inference comparator: Section~6.2, Assumptions~4--6, and Corollary~3 treat smooth continuous empirical quantiles with ridge regularization and a donor-dilution condition, not fixed-donor atomic post cells with local collisions, faces, and pulse-sharp cross-term control. Zhang, Zhang, and Zhang study DSC prediction and weight rates under quantile-grid and interior-weight conditions, which informs but does not settle the present cell-sampling experiment with finite-array curvature \(H_\ell\) and local-subsequence limit \(H\). Sommerfeld and Munk derive directional limits for empirical finite-space Wasserstein distances, supplying the atomic-transport precedent without a generated DSC barycenter. Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, Melly, and Wuthrich project simultaneous distribution-function bands into honest discrete quantile and quantile-effect bands; the DKW fallback uses that coverage logic but targets a learned-weight simultaneous \(L^2\) ball. Andrews supplies tangent-cone extremum asymptotics, and Canen and Song supply uniformly valid simplex-weight inference; neither composes the face projection, endpoint energy, and vanishing cross vector. Andrews and Mikusheva condition on Gaussian nuisance statistics, while Cox and Shi enumerate active constraints; these techniques inform the conditional experiment and certification but do not give its compound-loss cutoff. Robins and van der Vaart and Hoffmann and Nickl establish general honesty-versus-adaptation obstructions; the Bernoulli theorem computes the exact penalty for this collision experiment. Zhai et al. are the same-question consumer: their abundance analysis smooths discrete quantiles and reports pointwise percentile-bootstrap intervals, whereas this project targets the raw discrete post-treatment contrast between the observed intervention law and the donor-identified no-intervention law with simultaneous \(L^2\) coverage; their separate binary CDF and \(W_1\) elimination analysis is outside scope.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The local criterion minimizes only the common deterministic conditional squared-radius cutoff over \(\mathscr C_\eta\); it does not optimize expected radius, randomized rules, or arbitrary observation-dependent radius rules. The finite Gaussian object is a conditional loss experiment, not an unrestricted deficiency equivalence for the raw samples. The general oracle calculation uses the normalized leading loss \((1-\omega)A_t(V_h)+\omega\Psi_t(d,Z)\); the sharper cross term is nondegenerate only at its own finer scale and therefore does not alter that cutoff algorithm. The calculation retains exactly observed within-cell offsets and treats cross-cell translations and face offsets as nuisance. The DKW ball proves honest rate attainment, while feasible sharp conditional calibration remains open. Applying the result to Zhai et al. would additionally require a bridge for discrete pre-period outcomes, beta-weighted quantile fitting, period aggregation, spatial dependence, and interpolation.
body.honest_scope: The exact endpoint identity, exact six-term finite-array squared-error decomposition, pulse-sharp bound and joint local limit for \(B_{t,\ell}\), diagonal local compactification with \(H_\ell\to H\), normalized compound loss, coupled three-phase limits, component degeneracy criteria, exact known-weight and point-mass reductions, DKW upper rate, matching worst-case rate lower bound, Bernoulli honesty penalty, deterministic oracle cutoff, and legal \(J=2\), \(S=2\), \(D=2\) certificate are theorem targets. The cross contribution can be nondegenerate at its own \(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}\) scale but vanishes from every headline loss normalization. The stable-span model identifies \(Q^N_{0t,\ell}\) with the same \(w_\ell\) for every pre-treatment period and every post-treatment no-intervention period; it never equates that counterfactual law with \(Q^I_{0t,\ell}\). Feasible attainment of the conditional cutoff across changing support, covariance rank, and simplex face is explicitly open. Within-cell local offsets are conditioned on as exactly observed coordinates; cross-cell translations and face offsets remain nuisance. Oracle calibration is claimed only on fixed separated interior strata with continuous nondegenerate critical laws. If all relevant post laws are point masses, \(\Psi_t=0\) and the limit reduces to the standard tangent-cone quadratic; with known weights, the quadratic and every generated-weight cross or remainder term vanish and the result reduces to a finite-support empirical quantile law. In the one-donor Bernoulli restriction, \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell=1\), so all weight and cross terms are identically zero.
